scope: Bounded Linux Intel Chromium playback investigation, not a full release validation
conclusion: The previously failing playback gate did not reproduce on current Next with a quiescent host. Both unchanged playback runs and all three standard benchmarks passed. No causal software bottleneck or physical GPU fault is established by these results.

allowed_runs: if baseline passes: standard three hardware benchmarks, then one unchanged playback consistency repeat
if a playback acceptance run fails: one profile and at most one evidence-directed diagnostic control

host.initial_competing_work: Independent demo QA used 6–8 CPU cores with SwiftShader. User instructed waiting; those processes were not interrupted. Timing began only after they ended.

limitations: The 50-suite browser inventory, complete Rust matrix and native Linux GUI were not rerun; this is the requested bounded follow-up.
Chromium results are not native WebKit frame-rate evidence, Mac/Windows validation or a physical GPU health test.
The earlier failed pacing result is preserved in the previous investigation; the current passes do not establish why that older result failed.
Current source and host conditions differ from the previous failing run, so earlier contention is not established as its cause.

At 100,000 input rows, focus/orbit/full-range playback measure about 30–32 FPS at the 20,000-point budget and 12–14 FPS at 100,000 points. The existing benchmark assertions have no 60-FPS floor; a passed benchmark does not imply 60 FPS.

The million-row scale suite retains a legacy hardcoded softwareRenderer=true field and SwiftShader limitation text. Its runtime receipt records Vulkan under the Intel-only ICD; unlike playback and the two performance suites, the scale suite does not query the unmasked WebGL renderer. Raw evidence is preserved without relabeling it.
No renderer settings, budgets, thresholds, timing windows or product behavior were changed in this follow-up. No Radeon test/reset/rebind, hosted workflow, reboot or Public promotion was performed.
